question: The South Indian counterpart of the North Indian instrument 'Nagada' is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chenda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** nagara **or **naghara **is a **drum **used in the **Middle East**.
 
• There are **several types **of **naghara**, which are considered to be **the lead instrument in folk ceremonies **and **weddings**.
 
• **Nagada **(Indian Drum) is **a percussion instrument **used for **its rhythmic sounds**.
 
• **Nakara **is a **festival instrument **mostly used in **South Indian Hindu temples**.
 
• The **size may vary **and **this instrument **may be kept **near the entrance of the South Indian Hindu temples**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Been:**

 
 
• **​**The Been is also called pungi.
 
• It is a simple folk instrument traditionally played by snake charmers.
 
• It is made of a small gourd with a blowing hole at the top and two attached pipes at the bottom.
 
• Its sharp, penetrating sound is produced by reeds for each pipe inside the gourd.
 
 
 
• **Uddukai:**
 
 
• **​**The udukkai is a member of the family of membranophone percussion instruments of India and Nepal.
 
• It is used in folk music and prayers in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Its shape is similar to other Indian hourglass drums, having a small snare stretched over one side.
 
• It is made of wood or brass and is very portable.
 
• It originated in Tamil Nadu as well.
 
 
 
• **Damru**:
 
 
• A damaru is a small two-headed drum, used in Hinduism and Tibetan Buddhism.
 
• In Hinduism, the damaru is known as the instrument of the deity Shiva, associated with Tantric traditions.
 
• It is said to be created by Shiva to produce spiritual sounds by which the whole universe has been created and regulated.
